title: Runtime E: OpenAI's ChatGPT through the Airline Connector
lede: ChatGPT reaches the same Airline Connector as Meta's Muse (runtime B). What differs: who adds it, how it gets a client ID, which PingOne app signs Sam in, and who calls /mcp. Not tried yet: ChatGPT's PingOne app is not in MUSE_CONNECTOR_AGENTS on SE yet.

lanes.label: E. OpenAI's ChatGPT: the company adds the connector once, Sam just connects

nodes.label: 1. The company adds it once
sub: Admin: Workspace settings > Apps > Drafts > Publish
or an Apps SDK app listed in the app directory

nodes.label: 2. Sam asks in ChatGPT
sub: "How many airline points do I have?"

nodes.label: 3. ChatGPT picks the tool
sub: Sam picked the Airline app in the composer

nodes.label: 4. /mcp answers 401
sub: metadata points at /connector/authorize (PKCE S256, scope mcp)

nodes.label: 5. ChatGPT gets a client ID
sub: registers itself, or the admin pastes a client ID
callback: the one ChatGPT shows when the app is created

nodes.label: 6. PingOne sign-in
sub: the "ChatGPT agent login" PingOne app, picked by callback host chatgpt.com
same DaVinci flow, login hint ends .conn

nodes.label: 7. Protect: AI agent detected
sub: Protect names ChatGPT from its app id
the screen says how it knows

nodes.label: 8. Sam consents
sub: the flow picks it from the app id

nodes.label: 9. Muse gives ChatGPT its own token
sub: the PingOne token never leaves Muse

nodes.label: 10. /mcp call, gateway decides
sub: points and tier come back to ChatGPT

steps.title: Ready to use
steps.what: The company has already added the connector: Admin: Workspace settings > Apps > Drafts > Publish; or an Apps SDK app listed in the app directory.
steps.why: Members then only click Connect. Nobody types a URL or client ID.

steps.title: Ask
steps.what: Sam asks ChatGPT: "How many airline points do I have?".

steps.title: Call, no token
steps.what: ChatGPT picks loyalty_balance from the Airline Connector and calls /mcp. It has no token yet.
steps.why: The model chooses from the tool names and descriptions. The airline's name in them is what steers it.

steps.title: 401, sign in
steps.what: /mcp answers 401 with metadata: sign in at /connector/authorize, PKCE S256, scope mcp.
steps.why: ChatGPT learns where to sign in from the server, not from config.

steps.title: Authorize
steps.what: ChatGPT registers itself, or the admin pastes a client ID, then sends Sam to /connector/authorize. Muse starts the PingOne sign-in with the "ChatGPT agent login" PingOne app, chosen because the callback host is chatgpt.com.
steps.why: chatgpt.com is a listed agent host (MUSE_CONNECTOR_AGENTS), so it may register.

steps.title: Protect check
steps.what: PingOne runs the DaVinci flow: password, Protect risk, MFA on medium risk. Protect sees the "ChatGPT agent login" PingOne app and names ChatGPT.
steps.why: The agent is recognised by PingOne, not by its own word. The screen must say how it knows. Protect's museAgentClient predictor already lists that app (HIGH).

steps.title: Consent
steps.what: PingOne shows the "AI agent detected" screen, then asks Sam to let ChatGPT act for him. Sam agrees.
steps.why: No consent, no token: a "no" ends the flow with nothing issued.

steps.title: Exchanges, token
steps.what: Muse does the code swap and both exchanges with the "ChatGPT agent login" PingOne app, then gives ChatGPT its own access token at /connector/token.
steps.why: So act names ChatGPT. The PingOne token never leaves Muse. ChatGPT holds only a Muse token for scope mcp.

steps.title: Call with token
steps.what: OpenAI's servers call /mcp with that token. Muse calls the gateway, which checks the delegated token, and the points come back.
steps.why: Not tried yet: ChatGPT's PingOne app is not in MUSE_CONNECTOR_AGENTS on SE yet.
